text:
jordan: Quick follow-up from the RFC — proposal to push pilot/canary decisioning down into a lightweight local controller per runtime shard. Goal: faster rollbacks, fewer central hops, simpler backpressure when a variant misbehaves.
anya: digging this. main worry is consistency of telemetry signals across shards. how do we avoid noisy local decisions?
mike: we could require a minimum quorum of shard-level probes before flipping state. local controller proposes, central arbiter confirms if signals conflict.
sophia: sounds reasonable. what signals are we using? latency p50/p95, error-rate, hallucination/regression evals?
jordan: p50+p95, 5xx rate, and a light weighted regression score from the eval pipeline (sampled). also want to surface token-level stalls.
anya: sampling is key — keep probe footprints tiny. maybe default 1% of traffic for regression checks, adjustable per customer.
mike: tradeoff: local decisions reduce latency but increase ttv (time-to-detect cross-shard anomalies). propose: local fast-fail for clear-cut thresholds, fallback to central consensus for ambiguous cases.
sophia: how do we handle rollback loops? e.g., shard A flips, shard B follows, then central flips back — flapping. need hysteresis and cooldown windows.
jordan: agree. implement exponential backoff cooldown + sticky minimum window (e.g., 5m) before another change. also require a decaying penalty score to avoid oscillation.
anya: operational visibility? we need per-customer audit logs of decisions and the raw probe values. storage cost could grow.
mike: keep raw samples ephemeral (1h) and store decision events as compact records (who, why, probes summary) longer term. add an opt-in extended retention for compliance.
sophia: API surface: local controller should expose a tiny decision proto: {variant, action, reason_code, probe_snapshot_id}. sync with central for reconciliation.
jordan: rough proto ok. also want an opt-in dry-run mode where local controller only proposes and central logs what would have happened. useful for gradual rollout.
anya: testing: we need chaos/ftests for split-brain scenarios and for long-tail network partitions. add a canary that runs under degraded network during staging.
mike: deploy-bot: rolling canary will run with local-controller enabled on 5% of nodes in staging. tag: pilot-local-controller-01 :rocket:
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled at 2026-04-02T15:00Z.
sophia: action items: 1) jordan draft proto + backoff/hysteresis rules (PR), 2) mike simulate quorum heuristics in simulator, 3) anya spec telemetry retention opt-ins. I'll own follow-up doc.
jordan: will open PR with interface sketch and a paper-plan for simulation. thanks all. :thumbsup:
